instructions:
puppet desktop-control MCP (Windows). Background-safe by default: every acting tool takes a `target` selector {hwnd?,pid?,exe?,appId?,titleContains?,className?} that resolves ONE window for the call and is revalidated before every action. No cursor movement, no keyboard injection into the owner's session, no focus stealing, no raised window, whether the target is foreground or alt-tabbed. An ambiguous or vanished target is a typed error (ambiguous_target / target_gone). There is no escalation path: the allow_foreground:true, allow_cursor:true and allow_clipboard:true options are accepted by the schema and refused by the policy, so a refused call touches nothing.

Tools (one line each):
- screenshot: capture the whole virtual desktop (display=-1), one monitor, a window (window=<selector> or target={...}) or a region, without activating the window; returns the image, source{x,y,w,h}, scale, the monitor list and the image-to-screen formula
- diff: compare two captures (base/next: window selector, file path or the previous capture) pixel by pixel; returns changed, total, ratio, bbox, identical and the optional diff image
- list_windows: read-only visible top-level windows (hwnd/pid/exe/title/rects/elevated); never changes focus
- window: move|resize|minimize|restore|close|topmost by selector, hwnd or target, all no-steal (SWP_NOACTIVATE / SW_SHOWMINNOACTIVE); focus and maximize are refused with no_foreground_policy because they take the foreground or cover a monitor
- do: BURST tool: one call runs an ordered actions[] batch against one target through UIA patterns first, then PostMessage/SendMessage; per-action ok, never aborts the rest
- cursor: read-only cursor position plus monitor rects
- elements: read-only structured UI elements for a window (target/title/hwnd; zero pixels, no focus change); each entry carries ref, fp, rect, offscreen and invokable

Coordinates: `do` x/y under a `target` are CLIENT-area physical pixels of that window, used as given; without a target they are virtual-desktop SCREEN pixels, converted with ScreenToClient; rects from `elements` and `list_windows` are always SCREEN pixels; a screenshot image pixel maps to screen with screen_x = source.x + round((img_x + 0.5) * source.w / image.w) and the same for y.

Verbs by delivery class:
- posted (window messages to the locked target): click, down, up, drag, scroll, type, key, hotkey
- pattern (UIA patterns on the locked target): click with an element, scroll with an element, invoke with an element
- read (nothing is delivered): wait, wait_for, clipboard_get
- refused (no flag unlocks them): move (no_cursor_policy), type with an element (background_unavailable), focus_window (no_foreground_policy), set_value (background_unavailable), clipboard_set (no_clipboard_policy)

Invariants:
- I1: SendInput, SetCursorPos, SetForegroundWindow, BringWindowToTop and mouse_event have no call site anywhere: the mechanism to steal cannot be called
- I2: every refusal happens before anything is sent, under dry_run too
- I3: the target lock is revalidated before every action, so a vanished or replaced window refuses instead of being driven
- I4: nothing falls back to the foreground window: without a target an acting verb refuses
- I5: the server never elevates itself and never escalates a permission
- I6: a property that never appears means the control has no such pattern, never that it is false

Limits:
- bursts: a burst is not atomic across a service restart: actions already sent are not undone, so keep bursts short and idempotent
- ok_vs_effect: `ok` means the action was delivered, never that the target acted: read `effect` for what actually happened
- fp_scope: `fp` is identity, never state: rect, text and control state (checked, selected, expanded, range) do not participate, so an fp match means the same control properties (role, name, auto_id, invokable) and not the same condition - and not uniqueness either: a replacement control carrying those same four properties hashes the same, so a match never proves the control is the one you saw; a state-sensitive action needs a readback (effect, satisfied_by), never a fingerprint
- wait_for: `satisfied` is the condition's verdict and `ok` is the action's delivery: a timed-out wait_for reports satisfied:false with ok:true
- clipboard: clipboard_get truncates text past 1048576 chars and reports truncated:true
- pointer: the pointer is never in the pixels - neither capture backend composites it; `cursor{x,y}` is a position report
- ime: IME, dead-key and AltGr composition are not supported: there is no composition path on posted WM_CHAR
- touch: touch, pen and stylus input are not supported: there is no schema surface and no way to synthesize it in the background
- drag_and_drop: cross-window drag-and-drop is not supported: drag is three posted messages to one window
- clamping: a point outside the target client rect is posted into client message space and lands nowhere
- hdr: captures are SDR-composited, untagged bytes: there is no HDR or wide-gamut conversion
- raw_input: an app reading raw input (DirectInput) ignores posted messages and cannot be driven
- elevation: an elevated target cannot be driven: the refusal is typed and the server never elevates itself

Error codes (every code the server can emit): ambiguous_target, ambiguous_window, background_unavailable, bad_coordinates, bad_display, bad_out, bad_region, bad_target, bad_window, burst_budget_exceeded, capture_failed, capture_timeout, capture_unavailable, empty_crop, expect_fp_required, no_clipboard_policy, no_cursor_policy, no_foreground_policy, offscreen_element, size_mismatch, stale_ref, target_gone, target_required, uia_timeout, uipi_blocked, window_minimized.
dry_run=true validates exactly like the live call (every policy refusal included) but posts nothing.
